sections.name: File setup, TYPE_OPTIONS, CATEGORY_OPTIONS, TIER_LABELS
sections.title: Imports and fixed option lists
sections.what: Brings in the tools the page needs and defines the choices for source type (RSS, DOMAIN, API), category (news, regulatory, industry, association, company) and the five tier labels shown on screen.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the allowed values in one place so the form and the labels stay consistent.
sections.watch_out: These lists must match the values the server accepts, or saved sources will be rejected or shown wrongly.

sections.name: REGION_LABELS
sections.title: Region name lookup
sections.what: Maps internal region codes such as NORTH_AMERICA to short display names such as N. America.
sections.why: Likely reason: stores short labels for showing regions compactly. Where it is used is not visible in this section.
sections.watch_out: A region code missing from this list will show its raw code instead of a name.

sections.name: Sources (part 1)
sections.title: Page state, data loading and save actions
sections.what: Sets up what the page remembers, including the open forms, filters, sort order and new source draft. It loads the source list for the current industry and the source packs when that panel is opened. It also defines the actions to create, switch on or off, and save a source.
sections.why: Likely reason: the page changes often as the user filters, sorts and edits, so these values are kept in memory and refreshed from the server after each change.
sections.watch_out: After each create, toggle or save, the list is refreshed through the query cache. If that refresh is skipped, the screen shows stale data while the server holds the new values.

sections.name: Sources (part 2)
sections.title: Import, sorting and status setup
sections.what: Sets up the logic the page needs. It defines the bulk import action for source packs, loads the search provider status, sorts the source list when a column header is clicked, and starts row editing.
sections.why: Likely reason: the page keeps its logic here so the layout below only has to show results.
sections.watch_out: Sorting compares raw values directly, so mixed or missing values can land in an odd order.

sections.name: Sources (part 3)
sections.title: Page header and provider status panel
sections.what: Draws the top of the page: the title with a source count, the Source Packs and Add Source buttons, and a panel showing each search provider as ONLINE or OFFLINE.
sections.why: Likely reason: a quick health check at the top lets the owner see if search providers are down before importing.
sections.watch_out: The provider panel only appears when status data loads, so a failed status request simply hides it.

sections.name: Sources (part 4)
sections.title: Source packs panel and pack cards
sections.what: Shows the wind register on the renewables industry only. When Source Packs is open, it lists each pack as a card with its total, how many are new, and how many already exist, or a message if there are none.
sections.why: Likely reason: the pack cards show what an import would add before the owner clicks anything.
sections.watch_out: The import button depends on the new count, so a wrong count gives a wrong button state.

sections.name: Sources (part 5)
sections.title: Import button labels and add form start
sections.what: Sets the label on each pack's import button: importing, all already imported, or ready with the number of new sources. After an import it shows how many were imported and skipped. Then it lays out the first add-form fields: ID, name, type, URL and tier.
sections.why: Likely reason: the labels tell the owner what the button will do before and after a click.
sections.watch_out: The import result appears to be held only in page memory, so a reload clears it.

sections.name: Sources (part 6)
sections.title: Add form finish and filter dropdowns
sections.what: Finishes the add-source form with the tier and category choices, then Save and Cancel buttons. Save stays off until ID, name and URL have text. Also shows the filter dropdowns for source type and enabled status.
sections.why: Likely reason: Save is disabled until the required fields are filled so an incomplete source is not created.
sections.watch_out: The table is built from the full source list, so the filter dropdowns may not narrow rows unless filtering happens in the data request.

sections.name: Sources (part 7)
sections.title: Loading message and table header
sections.what: Shows a loading message while sources load, then starts the table. Name, Type, Tier and Category headers can be clicked to sort; URL, Region and Actions cannot.
sections.why: Likely reason: the loading message stops an empty table from looking like there are no sources.
sections.watch_out: Only four columns can be sorted, so the URL, Region and Actions columns will not change order when clicked.

sections.name: Sources (part 8)
sections.title: Name, type and URL cells
sections.what: Shows each row's name, type badge and URL as text, or as input fields when that row is being edited. RSS and API types get their own colors, and the URL opens in a new tab. Also starts the tier cell.
sections.why: Likely reason: the row switches into input fields so one row can be edited without leaving the table.
sections.watch_out: The link uses the saved URL exactly as stored, so a bad or unexpected address becomes a clickable link.

sections.name: Sources (part 9)
sections.title: Tier, category, region and row actions
sections.what: Shows the tier badge (tier 1 stands out most), the category, and a region label with a map pin. Then shows the row's action buttons: Save and Cancel while editing, or Edit otherwise. Closes the table.
sections.why: Likely reason: the edit buttons sit at the end of each row so the owner can save or discard one change at a time.
sections.watch_out: Region shows the raw code when no label exists, and Save sends the edit values without any check in this section.

sections.name: Sources (part 10)
sections.title: Closing the page layout
sections.what: Closes the page layout and the component. It adds nothing visible on its own.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

summary: Admin page for managing the list of news and reference sources the app reads, including adding sources, switching them on or off, editing them and importing ready-made source packs, based on the first 76 lines of the file.
purpose: Lets the team see every source the app can read, decide which are used, and add or import new ones for the industry currently selected.
why: Likely reason: the list of sources controls what information the app collects, so keeping it on one admin page makes it easy to review and change. Reason for the default sort by authority tier is not stated in the code.
how: First the page reads the selected industry from the app context. It then loads sources that match the type, enabled and industry filters. Ready-made source packs are loaded only when the packs panel is opened. Creating, switching on or off, and saving edits each send a request to the server, then refresh the source list. The rest of the page, from line 77 on, was not provided and is not described here.
inputs: Type and enabled filters, sort field and direction, the new source form (id, name, type, url, authority tier, category), edits to existing rows, and the selected industry.
outputs: A filtered, sorted list of sources on screen, and changes sent to the server when a source is created, switched on or off, edited or imported.
risks: Changes go straight to the live source list, so a wrong URL, type or tier changes what the app reads. Create, toggle and save requests show no error handling in the visible code.
debug: If the list is empty, check the type, enabled and industry filters first. If a change does not appear, check whether the server accepted the request and whether the list was refreshed. Lines 77 to 522 were not reviewed, so issues in the rest of the page cannot be ruled out.
